description: Use this when you need an organic swept solid whose cross-section changes along its length — a tapering body, horn, bottle, fairing, or duct — authored as a variable-section sweep along a spine. Insert a `variableSweep(spine, sections, opts?)` declaration into the user's .kcad.ts immediately before the last top-level return. The result is a Shape — chain `.translate(...)`, `.union(...)`, etc. via `add_feature`. `spine_binding` references an existing variable (Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[]) in the source; each `sections[i].profile_binding` references an existing Sketch. Sections must be strictly increasing in `t` and span [0, 1]; first t=0, last t=1. Orientation is not exposed by this MCP tool until runtime orientation support is wired. Validates every binding exists in the source via regex before inserting (fast structured error vs capture-time stack). Returns the modified code + diagnostics. Side-effect-free.

binding_name.description: JS const name for the new Shape binding (default: _sweep_<N>).

sections.description: Varying cross-sections along the spine; at least 2 entries, strictly increasing in `t`, first t=0, last t=1.

profile_binding.description: Existing Sketch variable name for this section.

spine_binding.description: Existing variable name for a Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[] declared earlier in the source.

name: add_variable_sweep

binding_name.description: JS const name bound to the new construct (when one was created).

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics from re-evaluating the modified source.

error.description: Failure message (present when ok is false).

new_code.description: Modified .kcad.ts source (present on success). Caller persists it.

ok.description: Whether the edit applied and re-evaluated cleanly.

title: Add Variable Sweep
